subject.title: Stuck-session liveness monitor misclassifies healthy processing runs as stale during event-loop stalls

question: Should OpenClaw change processing/no-activeWorkKind stuck-session recovery now, or require live/deterministic proof that healthy active runs can lose activity bookkeeping during event-loop stalls before changing the policy?
rationale: The source path exists and the current tests intentionally cover it, but the issue body still labels the healthy-run abort chain as likely rather than confirmed.

options.title: Require proof first
options.body: Keep this issue open until a controlled log, harness, or live run shows state=processing, classification=stale_session_state, and abort_embedded_run for a healthy in-flight run.

options.title: Patch classifier now
options.body: Approve a narrow policy change that treats processing/no-activeWorkKind as observe-only or long-running while redesigning stale-processing recovery tests.

options.title: Fold into broader liveness work
options.body: Handle this as part of the adjacent stuck-session/event-loop recovery cluster rather than as a standalone classifier edge.

recommendation.title: Require proof first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until a controlled log, harness, or live run shows state=processing, classification=stale_session_state, and abort_embedded_run for a healthy in-flight run.

likelyOwner.reason: obviyus has the most recent direct work on ownerless stalled-lane recovery, which is the policy area this decision would change.
